title: ForAllValues:StringNotLike
question: Does ForAllValues:StringNotLike follow its definitions, as the analyzer does, or the evaluation table under AWS's aws:ResourceOrgPaths example, which says the opposite in all three rows? The example's Deny is copied word for word, beside an Allow for all of S3.

cases.name: sportsou_costcenter
cases.description: The table's first row: the table says Match.

readings.ALLOW: the definitions: the path matches sportsou/*, so the condition fails and the Deny doesn't apply

cases.name: mediaou_costcenter
cases.description: The table's second row: the table says No match.

readings.EXPLICIT_DENY: the definitions: the path matches neither pattern, so the condition holds

cases.name: no_resource_org_paths
cases.description: The table's third row, with no aws:ResourceOrgPaths: the table says No match.

readings.EXPLICIT_DENY: the definitions: ForAllValues holds when the key is missing
readings.IMPLICIT_DENY: neither: the simulator's handling of a key left out of the call (see calibration)
